text:
ana: Quick heads-up — competitorX shipped "adaptive routing" yesterday. Sales already hearing asks. Do we want a parity response or double-down on our differentiators?

carla: saw it. One enterprise pilot asked for it this morning. They say tenant-level latency routing + model pinning is a must. They framed it as a blocker to sign.

derek: looked at their demo — seems like per-tenant routing + simple cost rules. We can ship a surface that covers 80% of asks without full infra changes by routing at the proxy layer and adding profile configs.

ben: eng view: full parity (routing infra, autoscale tie-ins, rollout policies) is ~3 sprints. A narrow MVP (tenant routing profiles + model pinning + canary fallback) is doable in 1 sprint if we scope carefully.

ana: propose two-track plan:
- Quick: ship "tenant routing profiles" + UI + model pinning + canary fallback as product toggle (2 weeks)
- Long: architect full adaptive routing with autoscaling hooks and per-tenant cost SLOs next quarter
Agree?

eve: PMM: fine, but messaging is key. For quick we should call it "tenant routing controls" and highlight SLA guarantees, not copy competitor language. Need launch criteria and target accounts for pilot.

carla: Sales: target accounts = AcmeCorp pilot + 2 other enterprise trials. They need audit logs + ability to pin a fallback model. If audit logs push timeline, pilot can accept telemetry only for initial trial.

ben: audit logs require schema + retention config — estimate +1 sprint. We can include minimal event logging (who changed profile, timestamp, routing decision id) in the MVP and call out full audit as GA item.

ana: okay. Draft MVP acceptance criteria:
```
- Tenant routing profile CRUD in Console
- Per-request routing decision recorded (decision_id) to telemetry
- Model pinning toggle per tenant with immediate effect
- Canary fallback policy: model fallback to default if target model unhealthy
- Rollout guard: opt-in toggle and per-tenant quota limits
- Pilot: enabled for AcmeCorp via feature flag
```

derek: ops question — who owns rollout runbook and rollback? I can draft canary playbook if eng agrees on telemetry hooks.

ben: yes, eng will own runbook + metrics. Need SLOs for latencies; will add token-level breakdown to console dashboards.

ana: next steps: ben to confirm sprint capacity by EOD, derek to draft canary runbook by tomorrow, eve to craft pilot messaging, carla to lock AcmeCorp pilot OK. I'll schedule 30m sync if any blockers.

deploy-bot: deploy queued for feature/tenant-routing-profiles -> staging :rocket:

carla: thanks — if we can get an internal demo by Friday that helps sales.

ana: will do. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
